subject: Question on data format for Stan in MCMCsuite

messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: Question on data format for Stan in MCMCsuite
parts:
Dear Nimblers,

First of all many thanks for a tool like Nimble.

I am using MCMCsuite to compare jags, winbugs, Nimble & Stan on the same model.

I have difficulties with Stan. My main difficulty is with the format of the data and init values that I provide to arguments stan_data and stan_inits respectively.

As an exemple for data I have tried putting in in a list:

ModelData_Stan<- list(Y = tabdivbm3$rssaprotot,x = tabdivbm3$volBMT, Ncases=length(as.factor(tabdivbm3$forest)),xsd = sd(tabdivbm3$volBMT), quantiles_main=quantile(tabdivbm3$volBMT,c(0.05,0.95)),
                    Nforests=nlevels(as.factor(tabdivbm3$forest)),forest=as.integer(as.factor(tabdivbm3$forest)),
                    Nper=tabdivbm3$nb.per.valid,meanlogNper=mean(log(tabdivbm3$nb.per.valid)),varlogNper=var(log(tabdivbm3$nb.per.valid)))


and then written it in a *.R file with the following commands:


format.data <- function (datalist){
    if (!is.list(datalist) || is.data.frame(datalist))
        stop("Argument to format.data must be a list.")
    n <- length(datalist)
    datalist.string <- as.list(rep(NA, n))
    for (i in 1:n) {
        if (length(datalist[[i]]) ==
            1)
            datalist.string[[i]] <- paste(names(datalist)[i],
                "=", as.character(datalist[[i]]), sep = "")
        if (is.vector(datalist[[i]]) & length(datalist[[i]]) >
            1)
            datalist.string[[i]] <- paste(names(datalist)[i],
                "=c(", paste(as.character(datalist[[i]]), collapse = ", "),
                ")", sep = "")
        if (is.array(datalist[[i]]))
            datalist.string[[i]] <- paste(names(datalist)[i],
                "= structure(.Data= c(", paste(as.character(as.vector(aperm(datalist[[i]]))),
                  collapse = ", "), "), .Dim=c(", paste(as.character(dim(datalist[[i]])),
                  collapse = ", "), "))", sep = "")
    }
  datalist.tofile <- paste("list(", paste(unlist(datalist.string),
        collapse = ", "), ")", sep = "")
    return(datalist.tofile)
}


cat(format.data(ModelData_Stan),file="Stan.data.R")

But it does not seem to work since I get the error message:
Error : variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=Nforests; base type=int

The command I use calling MCMCsuite is:

MCMCsuite_RStot.VBM_NBasPG_sigma4p_easa_P_v1_s3 <- MCMCsuite(code = modelCode,  constants = ModelConsts, inits = Inits[[1]], data = ModelData,
                thin = Thin, monitors = params, niter=Niter, burnin=Nburn,
                calculateEfficiency = TRUE, MCMCs = c("stan"),
                stan_model="modelCodeSTAN.stan",stan_inits="Stan.init.R",stan_data="Stan.data.R",makePlot=FALSE,
                debug=FALSE
                )



Any idea on where I went wrong?...

Sincerely,

Frédéric Gosselin

messages.author: 0ef2647ddd7095d7
messages.subject: Re: Question on data format for Stan in MCMCsuite
parts:
Hi Frédéric,

First, a couple of general comments: I think it is still the case that to call stan from nimble you will need to install nimble from our web site (see line of code to use at https://r-nimble.org/download).  Also, the feature to call the other packages together has encountered some bugs recently that appear to be due to registration of C functions in R from all the packages together.  Unfortunately we have not tracked that down yet.  If it becomes a problem, you may need to run each one separately rather than in one call to MCMCsuite or compareMCMCs.

Regarding your example: It is hard to diagnose without an example we can fully reproduce.  I will point you to the working MCMC comparisons from the examples page on our web-site.  Here is the first one: https://nature.berkeley.edu/~pdevalpine/MCMC_comparisons/some_BUGS_comparisons/blocker/nimble_blocker_comparisons.html
This is a little different than your case because it goes through compareMCMCs rather than MCMCsuite, but the former calls the latter, with inputs just arranged differently.  The example includes code to download the stan files needed from stan’s github repository and put them on your system.  You can compare to those files to see if you have your files set up and formatted correctly or if there is some other problem.

Perry

parts:
Thank you very much Perry for your useful answer. I will compare the formats and let you know. I have indeed installed Nimble form Nimble web page (actually I initially had the CRAN version but I had an error message telling me to install from Nimble web page, which I did).

If possible for the next versions, it would be very useful for readers as me to point to some pages like this one from the Nimble documentation to have examples.

And yes for the use of C functions within R on Windows (and possibly registration of C functions), I have also met some problems, both with Nimble and with other packages or functions. I reached the (temporary and probably false) conclusion that other libraries caused problems with C functions: especially when we use a second time the same C function (or something like this), then R can crash. I have never met this pb on Linux, with the same functions.

Sincerely,

Frédéric

messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: Re: Question on data format for Stan in MCMCsuite
parts:
Hi Perry,

based on your example I hink I have found a way to export data in list format (as in Nimble) to a R file to give the good format: this would be:

 file.remove("Stan.data.R")
 sapply(names(ModelData_Stan),function(xtotbbxugv,mylist)       {assign(xtotbbxugv,mylist[[xtotbbxugv]]);dump(xtotbbxugv, file = "Stan.data.R",append=T)},ModelData_Stan)
 

I hope it can help other users! For me unfortunately, it did not work due to initial values problems in Stan - Stan does not want to start with my initial values - but this is a Stan problem, not a Nimble one!

Thank you again,

Frédéric
